title: ‘बन्द ढोका र समय' कथामा भयानक रस [Terrible juice in the story 'Closed Doors and Time']
nepali: महेशविक्रम शाहको छापामारको छोरो (२०६३) कथासङ्ग्रहमा सङ्कलित ‘बन्द ढोका र समय’ भयानक रससँग सम्बन्धित कथा हो । यस कथामा २०५२ सालदेखि २०६२ /२०६३ सालसम्मको नेपाली समाजको अवस्थालाई विषयका रूपमा चयन गरिएको छ । यस कथामा विशेषत: ग्रामीण क्षेत्रमा बसोबास गर्ने आम नेपालीको अवस्था युद्धका वेलामा कतिसम्म कमजोर भएको थियो भन्ने विषयको उठान गरिएको छ । यहाँ ‘बन्द ढोका र समय’ कथामा रहेका विभाव, अनुभाव, व्यभिचारीभाव र स्थायीभावको निरूपण गरी रसाभिव्यक्तिको अवस्था विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । यस कथामा ऊ र नन्दा प्रमुख आलम्बनका रूपमा आएका छन् । त्यस्तै कथामा निनु, हतियारधारी, छोरी, रूपसराजस्ता आलम्बनको पनि उपस्थिति पाइन्छ । युद्धले ग्रसित नेपाली ग्रामीण समाज कथामा उद्दीपन विभावका रूपमा आएको छ । कथामा आएका यिनै आलम्बनका क्रिया कायिक, वाचिक, सात्त्विक तथा आहार्य अनुभाव बनेर प्रकट भएका छन् । यिनै अनुभावको शृङ्खलाबाट कथावस्तुको संरचना निर्मित भएको  छ । विश्लेष्य कथामा भय, शोक, वत्सल तथा जुगुप्सा भाव स्थायीभावका रूपमा प्रकट भएका छन् । यस कथामा चिन्ता, स्मृति, त्रास, पीडा, दैन्य, श्रम, आलस्य, आवेग, विबोध, धृति, विषाद, शङ्का, ग्लानि, औत्सुक्य, चपलता, जडता, वितर्क, अश्रु, संशय, मोह आदि व्यभिचारीभावहरू प्रकट भएका  छन् । यी सबै भावद्वारा परिपुष्ट बनेको भय स्थायीभाव भयानक रसका रूपमा अभिव्यक्त भएको छ ।
american_english: Collected in Mahesh Bikram Shah's short story anthology "Chhapamarko Chhoro" (2063 BS), "Banda Dhoka ra Samaya" is a story concerned with the terrible sentiment (bhayanaka rasa). In this story, the condition of Nepali society from the year 2052 BS to the year 2062/2063 BS has been selected as the subject. In this story, particularly the issue of how vulnerable the condition of ordinary Nepalis living in rural areas became during wartime is raised. Here, by determining the vibhava, anubhava, vyabhicharibhava, and sthayibhava present in the story "Banda Dhoka ra Samaya," the state of aesthetic expression (rasabhivyakti) is analyzed. In this story, U (He) and Nanda appear as the primary foundational determinants (alambana). Likewise, the presence of determinants (alambana) such as Ninu, the gunman, the daughter, and Rupasara is found in the story. The war-afflicted Nepali rural society appears in the story as the excitant determinant (uddipana vibhava). The actions of these very determinants appearing in the story are manifested as physical (kayika), verbal (vachika), involuntary (sattvika), and extrinsic (aharya) consequents (anubhava). The structure of the plot is constructed from the chain of these very consequents. In the story under analysis, the emotions of fear, grief, parental affection, and disgust are manifested as dominant emotions (sthayibhava). In this story, transitory emotions (vyabhicharibhava) such as anxiety, memory, terror, pain, wretchedness, fatigue, indolence, agitation, awakening, fortitude, melancholy, doubt, guilt, curiosity, fickleness, stupor, deliberation, tears, suspicion, and infatuation are manifested. The dominant emotion of fear, nourished by all these emotions, is expressed in the form of the terrible sentiment (bhayanaka rasa).
